# Model card: Policy check over the organisation's documents

| | |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Find which requirements of the organisation's own policy documents apply to an item, each with a quote. |
| Workflow | core (used by Pay) |
| Code | `pairly_core.policy.rag.check_against_policies`; Pay's spend policy check (`pairly_pay.checks.policy`) |
| Prompt | `core_policy_check` version `v1`, file SHA-256 `3d20e0a9ae8ed4ad...` |
| Output schema | `PolicyCheckOutput` |
| Model tiers, cheapest first | `small` (anthropic `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, openai `gpt-6-luna`) then `large` (anthropic `claude-sonnet-5-5`, openai `gpt-6.1-sol`) |
| Temperature | 0.0 |
| Output token limit | 2048 |
| Confidence threshold to accept | 0.6 |

## Inputs

The item's facts, the question, and the most relevant excerpts of the active policy documents (hybrid search), inside a delimited block with their markers neutralised.

## Outputs

`PolicyCheckOutput`: findings with the excerpt and quote they rely on. A finding whose quote is not in its excerpt is dropped and the outcome is at least `needs_review`.

## Human oversight

No policy found is not a pass. Errors, low confidence and rejected quotes send the item to a person.

## Limits

* Only as complete as the policy documents uploaded.
* Retrieval can miss a relevant excerpt.
* Every call is logged in `model_calls` (prompt version and hash, model, inputs, output, tokens, cost) and fails closed: no model means a person does the step.
